messages.content: What is LoRA?
LoRA fine-tunes small adapter matrices while keeping the base model frozen.
What is QLoRA?
QLoRA combines LoRA adapters with a 4-bit quantized base model to reduce memory use.
When should I use supervised fine-tuning?
Use supervised fine-tuning when you have examples of the inputs and responses you want the model to imitate.
Why keep evaluation examples separate?
Separate evaluation examples measure whether the model generalizes beyond the data it trained on.
What does an epoch mean?
One epoch is one complete pass through the training dataset.
What is gradient accumulation?
Gradient accumulation combines several small batches before updating weights, reducing peak memory use.
What is a checkpoint?
A checkpoint stores training state so a run can be inspected or resumed later.
Why use a small smoke test first?
A smoke test catches dataset, model, and memory problems before a long training run spends time and resources.
What is PEFT?
Parameter-efficient fine-tuning updates a small part of a model instead of every weight.
What is a Hugging Face adapter?
An adapter is a small set of learned weights loaded together with its original base model.
